title: worktree merge: honor uat_stop, invert the post-merge lane write, hold the worktree
action: The merge side of CONTEXT.md D4.1, D4.2, D4.3. Locate every anchor BY NAME, not by line number — usp-1 already edited phases.rs and the numbers have shifted. (1) D4.1 — the merge-time uat precondition (the block that refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING, today gated on uat_before_merge_config) now asks crate::uat::uat_stop_config. It refuses ONLY under UatStop::Merge; under Close and Off it does not refuse. A None from the reader keeps refusing the whole merge as an invalid-config error — keep the existing WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID code and widen its message to name BOTH keys and their legal values. Delete uat_before_merge_config from phases.rs once nothing calls it; its read now lives inside uat_stop_config. Keep --skip-uat working exactly as today under Merge. (2) D4.2 — close_the_lane_on_merge branches on the same resolved UatStop. Under Merge and Off, today's behavior is kept BYTE-FOR-BYTE: clear the waiting_on/run_state pair via clear_lane_waiting_on_pair and write the existing next_action naming bee close. Under Close, ask whether this feature's uat is still pending — reuse the same gate read the merge precondition uses (the live workflow record first, the default state record only as a same-feature fallback) and the lane rule crate::uat::uat_gate_applies_to_lane. If the lane cares AND uat is unapproved, do the INVERSE of today: set waiting_on kind gate, subject 'uat: <feature>', on the lane record, and write a next_action that names the road in one line — reload the product, test it, then either approve uat with bee gate --name uat --approved true, or fix in the worktree and merge again. If the lane is exempt, or uat is already approved, today's clear-and-point-at-close behavior is correct and stays. (3) D4.3 — while that uat wait is live, cleanup is forced OFF: --cleanup and config worktree_cleanup_on_merge true are both ignored, and the merge result carries one visible line saying why (the worktree is the only place a failed uat can be fixed; tearing it down drops the grant and the second merge would hit the no-granted-worktree refusal in handlers.rs). resolve_cleanup_on_merge in handlers.rs is the seam. --no-cleanup already means keep and is unaffected. (4) Preserve, and assert in tests, everything CONTEXT.md D5 says does not move: a merge NEVER writes lane phase; the lane write stays best-effort warn-never-fail (a failure warns, the merge stays green); ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE writes no lane change; MERGE_CONFLICT and WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT write nothing. (5) Tests in worktree/tests.rs: for each of the three uat_stop values, a merge of a standard-lane feature with uat unapproved and with uat approved; a tiny or small lane under close (exempt — clears, does not set the wait); the forced-cleanup-off case under close with both --cleanup and config true; a repeat merge after the wait is set (must still work, grant still present); and the four no-write paths from (4). Follow the existing fixture style in that file; note that a lane fixture file created UNTRACKED hides tracked-file behavior, so create it tracked where the assertion needs it.
done_when: Under uat_stop merge (and the uat_before_merge alias) every merge behavior is byte-identical to today. Under close a merge of a standard or high-risk feature with uat unapproved lands the code, sets the lane's waiting_on to the uat gate mark, writes a next_action naming reload-test-approve-or-fix-and-merge-again, and keeps the worktree even against --cleanup and config true. Under off nothing refuses and today's clear behavior holds. phase is never written, the lane write never turns a merge red, and the up-to-date, conflict, and proof-debt paths write nothing. The worktree suite is green.
notes: Phase 2. Depends on usp-1's crate::uat. Files are disjoint from usp-3 — the two run concurrently.

truths: uat_stop merge, and a repo carrying only the old uat_before_merge key, both behave exactly as bee does today.
Under close the merge no longer refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING.
Under close with the lane caring and uat unapproved, the merge SETS waiting_on kind gate subject 'uat: <feature>' instead of clearing it.
Under close the next_action names reloading and testing the product, and names both roads out: approve uat, or fix and merge again.
While that wait is live, --cleanup and worktree_cleanup_on_merge true are both ignored and the worktree survives.
A tiny, small, docs, or spike lane under close is exempt and keeps today's clearing behavior.
A merge never writes lane phase; the lane write stays warn-never-fail; up-to-date, conflict, and proof-debt paths write no lane change.

report.outcome: worktree merge honors uat_stop close/merge/off: merge-time precondition only refuses under Merge; under Close an unapproved standard/high-risk feature merges and SETS the lane waiting_on gate mark (reload/test/approve-or-fix) instead of clearing it; cleanup is forced off while that wait is live and the merge result names why; D5 no-write paths (phase, warn-never-fail, up-to-date, conflict, proof-debt) proven unchanged.
report.tests: PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml worktree — green — full declared worktree suite, the cells verify scope
deviations: handlers.rs listed in cell files but needed no edit: the D4.3 cleanup-suppression override lives in merge_finish (phases.rs), the point where the resolved uat-wait status is actually known; resolve_cleanup_on_merge itself needed no change since its bool output is what merge_finish overrides.

checks.truth: uat_stop merge, and a repo carrying only the old uat_before_merge key, both behave exactly as bee does today.
checks.evidence: packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/uat.rs:31 uat_stop_config — both keys absent => Some(Merge), uat_before_merge true => Merge, false => Off, non-boolean => None (same fail-closed shape the retired uat_before_merge_config had). phases.rs:317 `if uat_stop == UatStop::Merge && !skip_uat` is arithmetically the old `if uat_before_merge && !skip_uat`. phases.rs:498 close_the_lane_on_merge guards the new work behind `if uat_stop == UatStop::Close`; the fall-through body (clear_lane_waiting_on_pair + the bee-close next_action) is unchanged from the diff. phases.rs:786 `let effective_cleanup = cleanup && !uat_wait_set;` and uat_wait_set can only become true inside the Close branch, so Merge/Off reach attach_cleanup_outcome with the caller's exact cleanup bool. Only user-visible delta: WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID's message text widened to name both keys (phases.rs:310-315) — the code is unchanged and the widening is the cell's own instruction. cargo test --release worktree: 197 passed; full suite 2075 passed, 11 ignored.

checks.truth: Under close the merge no longer refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING.
checks.evidence: rg 'WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_PENDING' over crates/bee/src finds exactly one production site, phases.rs:327, and it sits inside the `uat_stop == UatStop::Merge` arm opened at phases.rs:317 — Close and Off never enter it. Proven live by tests.rs:3959 uat_stop_close_unapproved_standard_lane_merges_and_sets_the_uat_wait, which asserts answer.ok and result["merged"] == true with the gate unapproved.

checks.truth: Under close with the lane caring and uat unapproved, the merge SETS waiting_on kind gate subject 'uat: <feature>' instead of clearing it.
checks.evidence: phases.rs:498-503 — under Close, close_the_lane_on_merge re-runs uat_merge_precheck and, when precheck.lane_applies && !precheck.gate_approved, RETURNS set_lane_uat_wait_on_merge before ever reaching clear_lane_waiting_on_pair. phases.rs:544-551 inserts waiting_on = {kind:"gate", subject: format!("uat: {feature}"), asked_at, session: WORKTREE_MERGE_SESSIONLESS_ID}. Branch is reachable, not dead: tests.rs:3959 reads the lane back and asserts kind=="gate" and subject=="uat: demo".

checks.truth: Under close the next_action names reloading and testing the product, and names both roads out: approve uat, or fix and merge again.
checks.evidence: phases.rs:552 writes: "Merged into main at {short_sha}; reload the product and test \"{feature}\", then either approve uat (\"bee gate --name uat --approved true --lane {feature}\") or fix it in the worktree and merge again." The named command is real — `.bee/bin/bee gate --help` lists flags --name --merge --approved --lane. tests.rs:3959 asserts the text contains "reload", "approve uat", "merge again" and does NOT contain "bee close"; the same string is echoed on the merge result (result["next_action"]) and rendered by handlers.rs:merge_text_lines as a `next:` line.

checks.truth: While that wait is live, --cleanup and worktree_cleanup_on_merge true are both ignored and the worktree survives.
checks.evidence: phases.rs:786-800 — when `cleanup && uat_wait_set`, attach_cleanup_outcome is not called at all and a WORKTREE_MERGE_CLEANUP_SUPPRESSED_UAT_PENDING object is inserted instead; the only worktree remover is perform_cleanup, reached only from attach_cleanup_outcome (merge.rs:709-718). phases.rs:807 uses effective_cleanup so the suppressed merge also queues the keep-path cleanup deferral. Both entry points covered: tests.rs:4093 (flag, resolve_cleanup_on_merge(&main,true,false)) and tests.rs:4128 (config worktree_cleanup_on_merge:true) each assert created.worktree_root.exists() after the merge; tests.rs:4162 merges twice and gets ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE on the second rather than a no-granted-worktree refusal.

checks.truth: A tiny, small, docs, or spike lane under close is exempt and keeps today's clearing behavior.
checks.evidence: phases.rs:499 gates the SET branch on precheck.lane_applies, which is uat_gate_applies_to_lane(mode) at phases.rs:876 / uat.rs:57 — false for tiny/small/docs/spike, so a Close merge falls through to the unchanged clear-and-name-bee-close body. tests.rs:4066 uat_stop_close_tiny_lane_is_exempt_and_clears_the_lane asserts the cleared shape and a next_action naming "bee close --feature demo".

checks.truth: A merge never writes lane phase; the lane write stays warn-never-fail; up-to-date, conflict, and proof-debt paths write no lane change.

No-write paths: MERGE_CONFLICT (phases.rs:372) and ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE (phases.rs:406) both return StageOut::Done from merge_stage before Staged is built, so merge_finish's lane write is unreachable; WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT (phases.rs:165) is a zero-mutation refuse_merge. Byte-identity asserted by tests.rs:3542 (up-to-date) and the two new tests a_merge_conflict_leaves_the_lane_record_byte_identical and a_proof_debt_refusal_leaves_the_lane_record_byte_identical (tests.rs:~4200-4271), each comparing std::fs::read of the lane file before and after.
